sections.heading: What Furniture Assembly Involves
sections.body: Furniture assembly is the process of constructing a flat-pack or self-assembly unit from its component parts (boards, cam locks, dowels, hinges, and runners) in the correct sequence and orientation, achieving a result that is square, level, and structurally sound. The complexity varies considerably: a BILLY bookcase is a straightforward forty-five-minute job; a PAX wardrobe with internal fittings, soft-close hinges, and sliding doors is a three-hour project requiring precise hinge adjustment to ensure doors hang level and close flush. The most common assembly failures (furniture that wobbles, doors that sag, drawers that stick) are caused by incorrect cam-lock tightening, back panel incorrectly seated before the top is fixed, or a unit positioned on an uneven floor without compensation. A professional assembler avoids all of these outcomes as a matter of routine.

sections.heading: Common Assembly Challenges by Product Type
sections.body: IKEA PAX wardrobes are the most frequently assembled units we encounter in Salisbury homes, and they have a specific set of challenges: the hinge mounting plate must be positioned exactly to the millimetre for soft-close doors to seat correctly; the internal frame fittings (KOMPLEMENT drawers, pull-out trays) must be installed before the unit is stood up; and the anti-tip strap, which IKEA includes but many customers never fit, must be anchored to the wall stud, not just the plasterboard. KALLAX shelving units require wall anchoring as a safety requirement (tall units can topple with stored weight). BESTA media units with push-open or soft-close door mechanisms require precise hinge calibration. Chest of drawers from brands including Argos Habitat, Dunelm, and John Lewis flatpacks commonly suffer from drawer runners that bind if the carcass is even slightly out of square; this is prevented by assembling on a flat surface and checking diagonals before fitting the back panel.

sections.heading: How FixWell Assembles Furniture
sections.body: We begin every assembly job by checking the parts manifest against the physical contents, a step that identifies missing components before assembly begins, saving considerable time. We assemble in the correct sequence: base and side panels first, internal fittings and drawer runners before the back panel, back panel before the top. We use a spirit level on the floor to identify any significant rake before starting, using adjustable feet or furniture wedges to compensate on uneven Salisbury floorboards. Cam locks are tightened by feel rather than force; over-tightening splits the chipboard core and is irreversible. Hinges are adjusted in all three planes (height, depth, and lateral position) using the adjustment screws, achieving a consistent 2–3mm gap around each door. Anti-tip straps are anchored to wall studs wherever possible; we carry a stud finder to every assembly job as standard.

sections.heading: Time, Cost, and Popular Brands in Salisbury
sections.body: The Salisbury area is served by the Southampton and Eastleigh IKEA, with many Salisbury customers collecting flat-packs for same-day assembly. We work with all IKEA ranges (PAX, KALLAX, BESTA, HEMNES, BILLY, EKET, SEKTION kitchen units), all B&Q GoodHome and Goodhome Atomia ranges, Argos Habitat, Dunelm, Made.com, Wayfair, and any brand that comes with assembly instructions. Typical assembly times at our standard rate of £20–£40/hr: BILLY bookcase 45 min; HEMNES chest of drawers 60 min; PAX wardrobe (two-door, internal fittings) 2.5–3 hrs; BESTA media unit with doors 1.5 hrs. We can assemble multiple items in a single visit, making the booking more efficient. Most assembly jobs in Salisbury homes are completed in a half-day appointment.

faqs.q: Do you assemble IKEA furniture in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Yes. IKEA flatpack is the most common assembly job we carry out, including PAX wardrobes, KALLAX units, BESTA media cabinets, BILLY bookcases, and HEMNES furniture. We bring our own tools and work from the official IKEA assembly instructions.

faqs.q: Do you fix wardrobes and tall units to the wall?
faqs.a: Yes, and we strongly recommend it. Tall wardrobes and shelving units, particularly IKEA PAX and KALLAX, must be wall-anchored to prevent toppling. This is a safety requirement in homes with children. We use a stud finder to locate a fixing point in the wall and anchor the anti-tip strap or L-bracket correctly.

faqs.q: What if parts are missing from the box?
faqs.a: We check the parts manifest at the start of the job. If components are missing we advise you. IKEA provides replacement parts free of charge, and most other brands have a spare parts line. We are happy to return once parts arrive rather than attempting assembly with missing components.

faqs.q: Can you assemble furniture from brands other than IKEA?
faqs.a: Yes. We assemble furniture from all flat-pack brands including B&Q GoodHome, Argos Habitat, Dunelm, Wayfair, Made.com, Next, John Lewis, and any other brand that comes with assembly instructions.

faqs.q: How much does furniture assembly cost in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Our rate is £20–£40/hr. A single large wardrobe typically takes 2–3 hours; smaller items like a chest of drawers or bookcase take 45–60 minutes. Booking multiple items in one visit is the most cost-effective approach.

faqs.q: Do you take away the empty flat-pack boxes?
faqs.a: We flatten all packaging during assembly. Disposal is your responsibility, but we are happy to assist with moving packaging to a recycling point if needed. If you need a waste removal service we can advise local options in Salisbury.
